notes.title: Devlog #5 | Making Beautiful Top-down Worlds
notes.content:
Over our last 5 years developing Songs of Glimmerwick, we've made a lot of discoveries about making a top-down world. Things that make the world more beautiful, navigable, varied, and cohesive. This devlog is a behind-the-scenes look at all those discoveries. We also compare what it's like building for a fixed camera vs the "free" camera of our previous title [i]Eastshade[/i].

[previewyoutube=JPQ2NVwm1Xk;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Devlog #4 | World First Design and Time in Glimmerwick!
notes.content:
This devlog covers two topics: 

One is our world first design philosophy, where we put the world and sense of place before anything, including mechanics. This is backwards from the way most games are designed, but we like to think it's the unique DNA that makes our games unique. It's the philosophy we used to make our previous title [i]Eastshade[/i], and we are approaching Glimmerwick the same way.

The other is our approach to time in Glimmerwick. Time freezes during events, and every evening. We feel it relieves the time pressure felt in most farming sims, but still offers the ebb and flow of days and seasons, and offers us (the designers) more narrative and tonal control than the constant night day cycle common RPGs.

Enjoy much more detail on these topics, and a few more in the devlog!

[previewyoutube=FSqMeX4Ix80;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Devlog #3 is out and it's all about our characters!
notes.content:
Glimmerwick is a lively bustling place! There are currently over 100 unique characters and rising, and many of them are dynamic with schedules and some even change their outfits on occasion. In this devlog I give a rundown of what our character pipeline looks like, how we get them all rigged and animated, and some tricks for how we're able to create so many characters with a small team!

[previewyoutube=qTzuy8FEOeY;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Devlog #2 is now up!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

In this devlog we go on a deep dive into our art pipeline, and explore some really unique things about how we're creating the games visuals. It covers more technical topics compared to our first devlog, but if you love seeing behind the scenes on how games are made, grab a tea and enjoy the tour of our process!

notes.title: Starting a Video Devlog!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Development is going strong, but release is still a ways off. To tide you over in the meanwhile, we're starting a devlog! In this series of videos we'll cover what we've been up to, behind the scenes clips of our process, as well as some philosophy and just generally things we think about when designing the game. We hope you like it!

And please feel free to subscribe to our channel on YouTube if you want to catch the future devlogs! And of course liking and subscribing helps us out in the YouTube algorithm so we'd greatly appreciate it!

notes.title: Eastshade devs reveal a new witchy RPG mixing magic, music and gardening
notes.content:
If you're after a way to make your magic system seem cutesy yet different at the same time, music is a good one to go for. Sure, it's been done before, but it feels inherently charming. At least, it does in the trailer for newly-revealed Songs Of Glimmerwick, a new game from Eastshade Studios that promises to blend RPG, adventure, and gardening.

No specific release date is confirmed, aside from "next year". I have to give them credit for the name Songs Of Glimmerwick, which immediately lets you know that this will be about music and magic, and probably have an amount of tweeness. Specific tweeness levels unconfirmed but they're looking good from the trailer, where you can also clap eyes on some pretty cool-looking gardening, a tree telling you to stfu, and a man earnestly giving you a wooden flute as you head off to magic university.
